The "we're not done — this is overtime" defiance and the childhood-hero imagery track Shiho steeling against dismissive comments and, at the end, voicing her dream to headline such an arena through the band's own power.
EVENT|0162-find-the-dream-view.attribution: English translation by Shiru. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:Sympathy/Eve|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0164-choices-for-the-future.resonance: "All Save Challenge" pairs the resolve to save someone by breaking free of hazy, stagnant days with Emu's pledge to rescue Kikyogumi from disbandment. Its refrain of sewing up burst-open ideals and taking pride in failure — better shot down than stagnating — is the bold, openly experimental show format Emu and Suzu propose to a skeptical board. The lyric's insistence that nothing ripens in an instant yet "it's impossible for it not to come true" mirrors their turnaround gamble; the song's plea about forgiveness and unshakable belief underscores Suzu's hidden double life as chairman's granddaughter revealed at the climax.
EVENT|0164-choices-for-the-future.attribution: English Translation by Thai1210. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:オールセーブチャレンジ (All-Save Challenge)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0165-soshite-hari-ha-ugoki-dasu.resonance: "Mx.Nihil" is Mafuyu's numbness set to music: its coming-apart-at-the-seams emptiness and endless internal debate over expectations, test scores, and a love that hurts even when well-meant trace her slide back into pain as her mother relapses into control. The bitterly warm memory of the sponge-like shortcake that hurts to recall mirrors the remembered maternal warmth she can never quite reach. Its unresolved cry to just be loved without expectations, ending on "it hurts," matches the event's bleak coda — the mother catching herself, apologizing, yet privately agonizing as the painful cycle begins anew and Mafuyu returns to Nightcord's care.
EVENT|0165-soshite-hari-ha-ugoki-dasu.attribution: English translation by [https://x.com/kizudarakeni Tsuyuki]. May only be used in accordance with the restrictions stated on her [[User:Tsuyuki|user page]].

EVENT|0168-cheer-with-my-heart.resonance: "Eleventh" builds around a slanting clock hand and endless emotions that keep resounding — an image of persistent, unfading feeling that matches Arisawa's teaching that a "true idol" spreads hope simply by being herself. Its refusal to run from kindness and its note that brilliant things always sit beside sadness resonate with Airi's recollection of failed auditions, the bully she inspired, and Hiyori's lesson about putting others' smiles first. The refrain "it all starts from here" and the love she ascertained track Airi discovering Hiyori's motto traces back to Arisawa herself, deepening her resolve to give the Lumina Grand Prix everything.
EVENT|0168-cheer-with-my-heart.attribution: English translation by Violet Lights, with edits by MeaningfulUsername. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:イレヴンス (Eleventh)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0169-aim-higher-and-higher.resonance: "Voice of The Beam" is a beam of light meant to outshine the stars and pierce the world — the literal "top of the world" Vivid BAD SQUAD is chasing at SONIC NOTES. Its vow that there'll be no more days of giving up or singing head-down, and no more singing alone into a "BAD in the sky," mirrors the group finally grasping that the "world" means setting a global audience's hearts ablaze. The lyric's call to rise unafraid and start a "new legend," shining higher than that star, matches the ending where RaveN announces Lasting ECHO Fest and VBS vows to win RUSH BEATS onto that stage.
EVENT|0169-aim-higher-and-higher.attribution: English translation by Violet Lights, with edits by Violet. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:光線歌 (Kousenka)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0172-deeper-and-deeper.resonance: "Eyelid" burns with the resolve to use up the whole body and set oneself ablaze chasing an unknown, unseen beauty — Rui's hunger to close the nameless gap between his crowd-pleasing craft and Tom Gray's emotional depth. Its confession of not wanting to let any of it slip away, and the ghost of a taken role watching from above, mirror Rui confronting how he'd suppressed his own raw feelings to please the widest audience. The lyric's ache to reach a place "where I won't feel the cold" and to share a burden maps onto his monster show — a lonely creature who accepts himself yet asks to stay among the humans who accept him, winning Tom's praise.

EVENT|0173-unsteady-still-steady-step.resonance: "Transparent Palette" reframes indecision as grace: a palette still translucent that is "beautiful in its own way" and days of one-step-forward, one-step-back directionlessness capture Honami's paralysis between the solo show and the Fan Festival. The lyric's detour "on the way to the best days of our lives" and its refusal to settle for a stage someone else prepared echo her exhaustive research and desire to lead well. When the Fan Festival offer is rescinded and a future slot promised, the song's tender resolve to remember every feeling and take the longer way around mirrors Honami turning her flash of relief into a vow to grow decisive.
EVENT|0173-unsteady-still-steady-step.attribution: English translation by Shiru. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:透明なパレット (Toumei na Palette)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0174-start-rolling-stars-crossing.resonance: "Our Story As It Is" is a manifesto for unadorned sincerity — weaving "our story as it is" and discarding a lying mask because "I'm alright being myself" — which is exactly the lesson Minori learns after overtrying and stumbling on the Grand Prix's first day. Its wish to make someone's smile bloom and its embrace of staying clumsy track Haruka nominating her to represent the group "purely." The song's promise that together they can overcome the impossible and light a flame of hope mirrors the climax, where Minori's tearful, heartfelt praise turns the crowd around for the heckled Hikarin and wins her over.
EVENT|0174-start-rolling-stars-crossing.attribution: English translation by [[User:MK The Misery Kid|MK The Misery Kid]], with edits by MeaningfulUsername. May only be used in accordance to the restrictions stated on their [[User:MK The Misery Kid#Translation TOS|user page]].

EVENT|0175-competitive-fire.resonance: "Accelerate" pushes past "the crown of victory" with wings spread wide, learning to ride frustration for fun rather than resist it — the exhilarated momentum Vivid BAD SQUAD rides after watching RADder and setting their sights on RUSH BEATS. Its refusal to hold back because otherwise "both dreams and reality would get boring" and its belief in a never-before-seen blue sky far ahead mirror the group and their new rival teams igniting each other. The recurring image of a place they belong "tied together with singing voices" matches the ending, where An finds a true rival and illys and Embers rush to the airport, all vowing to reunite and compete.

EVENT|0177-hodokenu-ashita-ni-te-wo-noba.resonance: "Embellish" runs on the double meaning of dressing up: adorning one's sorrows and "atonements" so a heart can finally be filled, which mirrors Mizuki drifting without a dream while everyone around chases theirs. The song's turn from wounds left behind becoming "precious marks" to becoming someone who can love those wounds tracks Mizuki's arc from feeling left behind to glimpsing a purpose in protecting others' feelings. Its closing repetition of the title over an ordinary, accepted morning lands exactly where the story ends — with Yuki's gifted dress helping the hesitant customer reclaim a buried wish, and Mizuki finding that quiet, self-honoring beauty radiant.
EVENT|0177-hodokenu-ashita-ni-te-wo-noba.attribution: English translation by Rouse01. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:飾って (Kazatte)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0178-deep-dark-for-light.resonance: "Goodbye Heaven, Come Back to Hell" voices Prince Bless's despair as a swirl of unanswerable questions — devil or angel, heaven or hell — matching Tsukasa's struggle to feel a hopelessness he can't otherwise imagine. The recurring vow to protect even a clumsy, awkward weakness and grow stronger through shed tears frames his breakthrough: reaching genuine despair by picturing a world that rejects shows and smiles. The song's refusal to say a real "goodbye," swallowing the twisted shape instead, echoes the ending where the audience's cries pull Bless back and WxS earns its own stage rather than a clean defeat.

EVENT|0182-kun-to-tsunagu-heart-beat.resonance: "Star" reframes the act of being saved as also saving others — "I've been saved and also saved" — which is precisely what WITH becomes for Ichika as her thank-you to Miku ripples outward. The lyric's wish to be not a highlight in the darkness but a star in the middle of the world captures her realizing music's power to build community. The closing image of everyone holding stars "shining equally" matches the ending, where the viral song draws cover singers, illustrators, and classmates together into one connected world.
EVENT|0182-kun-to-tsunagu-heart-beat.attribution: English translation by Shiru, retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:スター (Star)/Daibakuhashin|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0183-majiwa-ru-iro-haano-nichi-nom.resonance: "If Your Sky Should Weep" is built on the plea to carry "half" of another's burden — to twine their chain and storm around oneself — which is exactly Shizuku's selfless move to coach the very rivals who once resented her. The lyric's ache to embrace the gloom that sneers at you maps onto her overhearing Cheerful*Days' lingering bitterness yet choosing to help anyway. Its image of sharing an umbrella's half resolves in the ending, where Alisa accepts Shizuku's help and old wounds heal into a respectful rivalry.
EVENT|0183-majiwa-ru-iro-haano-nichi-nom.attribution: English translation by MeaningfulUsername. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:あなたの空が泣くのなら (Anata no Sora ga Naku no Nara)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0184-colors-of-pure-sense.resonance: "The Name of That Painting is" turns a dream crushed under "the shadows of ideals" into something detested, mirroring Ena's block when safe, correct technique earns her last place. The insistence that there's no single correct answer and that she can paint over it "again and again" tracks her discovery that every attempt to ruin the Nightcord piece only deepens it. The song's final resolve to paint this SEKAI true to herself even if it isn't beautiful lands on the climax, where her real failure is failing to express — and her flawed, honest worldview becomes her weapon.
EVENT|0184-colors-of-pure-sense.attribution: English translation by Shiru. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:その絵の名前は (Sono E no Namae wa)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0185-choukoku-no-purotagonisuta.resonance: "GO FORTH" stages a battle between a haunting past hidden "deep within fate" and the command to face ahead — the exact shape of Nene's stage trauma versus the curtain she must walk through. The repeated cry that a wound-covered heart is "not weak anymore" and that damaged courage is enough mirrors Rui's tough-love gamble and the trust behind it. The song's driving chant of "go forth" under a watching world resolves in her stellar turn as Princess Heart, courage reclaimed precisely because her friends demanded it.
EVENT|0185-choukoku-no-purotagonisuta.attribution: English translation by Violet Lights, proofread by ElectricRaichu. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:征け (Yuke)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0187-overcome-one-s-limits.resonance: "Fighter" is all forward momentum — fire out your passion or it means nothing, disregard everything that says "impossible" — which is Akito's mandate to win over a hostile New York crowd in two weeks. The lyric's blunt "no time for complaining, go and struggle" and its shifting into high gear track his push through the language barrier via a bilingual song structure. The demand to walk the talk with real resolution rather than just words pays off in the ending, where his limit-breaking performance secures the No.9 Records contract.
EVENT|0187-overcome-one-s-limits.attribution: English translation by Thai1210. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:ファイター (Fighter)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0188-aogu-yozora-ni-hoshi-ha-magir.resonance: "Flower Knot" is a song of the unspoken — "I can't say it," mouth kept shut for fear everything would crumble — which is Saki's exact predicament as her true wish clashes with the band's rise. Its tension between clinging to "things that don't change" and chasing "more hope than now" mirrors her fear that intimate, close-up connection can't coexist with ever-larger stages. The lyric's true heart still "waiting for spring" while she panics and pretends not to notice matches the ending, where she buries those feelings to keep her place in Leo/need.
EVENT|0188-aogu-yozora-ni-hoshi-ha-magir.attribution: Official English translation retrieved from the [https://youtu.be/Wu8WtrTCX-Q original music video].

EVENT|0190-kono-monogatari-ha-kibou-wono.resonance: "Polar Star" opens on a lost compass in a blurred night sky — aimless drifting — which mirrors Haruka steering a randomly assembled team toward exam-stressed, depressed children with no obvious approach. The unfading star that always twinkles beside you, swallowing "anxiety and curses," becomes the reassurance she reshapes the whole event around: vulnerability and connection over high-energy spectacle. Its plea "find me, watch over me" so no one gets lost lands on the ending, where MORE MORE JUMP! becomes the children's guiding light and secures second place into the finals.
EVENT|0190-kono-monogatari-ha-kibou-wono.attribution: English translation by [[User:MK The Misery Kid|MK The Misery Kid]], with edits by [[User:Shiru-|Shiru]]. May only be used in accordance with the restrictions stated on their [[User:MK The Misery Kid#Translation TOS|user page]].

EVENT|0192-same-nai-gensou-wo-nokku-shit.resonance: "Love and Punishment" fixates on tangled threads and whether tearing them apart would bring relief — the very question of codependency Luka forces on Kanade about saving Mafuyu. The lyric's "barely believing we belong, emptily stroking each other's wounds" names the fear of losing one's place that Kanade's grandmother describes, while "if eventually our hands came undone" voices the option of separation. Its closing spiral — whose sake, what is best for your sake — mirrors the climax, where Kanade must face all three uncomfortable truths at once to find a real way forward.
EVENT|0192-same-nai-gensou-wo-nokku-shit.attribution: English translation by [[User:Shiru-|Shiru]], with edits by Violet.

EVENT|0193-go-all-out.resonance: "Permeating Warmth" trades in lukewarm, swaying temperature slowly overlapping into a shared heat — the wary, respectful heat that grows between Toya and his rival Slade. The lyric's refusal to say "this is for you" and its wish to be a fragment that melts the other's heart mirror Toya honoring Slade's demand for an unpitied, all-out battle and keeping his deafness secret. Its "unrefined heat" and voices echoing toward the future pay off in the ending, where Toya sings through a fever to give that limit-breaking performance and both teams leave with mutual respect.
EVENT|0193-go-all-out.attribution: English translation by Shiru. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:透過する温度 (Touka Suru Ondo)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0195-path-made-by-faith.resonance: "Let's go on, just like this" reframes a long road — blistered feet, no need to rush, footprints accumulating with every worn-down step — as Shiho's journey from the bass Sumire first taught her to a televised battle against her. The lyric's shift from "we believe" to "we want to believe," and its comfort that for every night of "we can't go on" they still met the morning, matches her intense preparation and growth. Its seeds sprouting even with no rainbow after the rain lands on the ending, where a fan letter reveals someone she inspired to pick up the bass — proof the path is real.

EVENT|0196-change-emuha-oujo-sama.resonance: "Beyond! Wonderpyoi" bounces off the contrast between a cramped castle of endless lessons and hidden true feelings against the urge to selfishly play and adventure — exactly Princess El's stifled life versus her secret theme-park dream. The song literally sings "swapping places, dreams come true" and "quit being a princess, I want to be myself," mirroring Emu's plan to trade identities so El can chase her goal. Its Cinderella imagery — throwing away the glass slipper, leaping from the pumpkin carriage — fits the ending where El stops playing her assigned role and boldly wins her father over to her own dream.
EVENT|0196-change-emuha-oujo-sama.attribution: Official English translation retrieved from [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:とびだせ！わんだぴょい (Tobidase! Wonderpyoi)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0198-open-up-new-horizons.resonance: "Colorful Foundation" frames Airi's transformation into the timid Michiru as a "bold foundation" and an ever-shifting "next phase" — the song's insistence that shape-shifting at will is a weapon rather than a disguise mirrors her method-acting gamble that identity is malleable, not fixed. Its refusal of any tidy ending and its vow to leap forward carrying contradictions echo the title's open horizons and Airi accepting a role that is the opposite of herself. The climactic image of a single spark scattering inner darkness into hope lands on Episode 7's continuous run-through, where her genuine tears of joy convert Mao's early prejudice into praise.
EVENT|0198-open-up-new-horizons.attribution: English translation by [[User:Treecar|Treecar]], proofread by MeaningfulUsername. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:カラフルファンデーション (Colorful Foundation)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0199-amid-the-wavering-light.resonance: "CONFESSION" carries the ache beneath Mizuki's private ultimatum with herself — its images of nurturing something that only wilts and measuring to exact specification only to have it "leak" mirror her grueling, deadline-bound attempt to draft and sew a dress while keeping up with Nightcord. The refrain that every step forward only hurts more yet resolving to keep walking maps onto the event's resolution, where Mafuyu and Miku tell her to pursue both fashion and music for as long as she can. Even its closing gratitude for a painful attachment echoes Mizuki choosing not to abandon either path despite the exhaustion.
EVENT|0199-amid-the-wavering-light.attribution: English translation by Mafuyu, with edits by Violet. Retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:告白 (Kokuhaku)/Naisho no Pierced|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0200-zanshou-no-inside-direction.resonance: "The Puppet's Reality" casts Rui as both puppeteer and director — its conceit of manipulating a performer like a spinning marionette to chase "dreams, ideals, and reality" mirrors his scheme to play off-camera antagonist and pull Nagamine's real anger into the role. The lyric where hidden, lied-about anger surfaces into darkness and is then reeled back by a thread tying two people together tracks Episode 7 exactly: Rui provokes the raw take, then apologizes and reconciles. The song's vow to breathe life into a "wondrous world" points to the ending's spark, with Director Ohara's praise leaving Rui inspired to build a bigger show for Wonderlands x Showtime.
EVENT|0200-zanshou-no-inside-direction.attribution: English translation by [[User:SunnySkiesTLs|SunnySkiesTLs]], proofread by [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:User:CoolMikeHatsune22|CoolMikeHatsune22]]. Can only be used in accordance to the restrictions stated on her [https://rentry.co/SunnySkiesTLs Rentry].

EVENT|0201-show-em-what-s-up.resonance: "CRASH THE PARTY" is itself the breakthrough An finds — its constant code-switching between Japanese and swaggering English enacts the very fusion of childhood street-song rhythm with English flow that lets VBS trade rigid grammatical correctness for raw feeling. Its boasts about being the baddest crashing the party and paving one's own road answer Ways' taunt that the group only rose through Elena's connections. The song's closing image of an undying bond as hellfire underscores the ending, where An's emotionally charged English rap flips a hostile crowd and earns both the qualifier win and Ways' respect.

EVENT|0202-yakusoku-no-passerelle.resonance: "Through the World" turns the event's premise — disparate members walking unfamiliar Sekai to reach one grieving girl — into its refrain about walking worlds no one else has known and chasing answers you cannot see. Its questions of "what will you write" and "where will it reach" mirror the girl's abandoned composition notebook and the very song the members build and deliver into her heart. The lyric admitting wounds that never fully heal yet resolving to keep going embodies the story's aim to depict "what lies beyond overcoming" grief, and the final vow to change the future's past from here lands on her awakening and her new goal to write music that reaches her grandmother.
EVENT|0202-yakusoku-no-passerelle.attribution: Official English translation retrieved from the [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:世界の歩き方 (Sekai no Arukikata)|Vocaloid Lyrics Wiki]].

EVENT|0203-atatakana-omoide-wo-tadotsu-t.resonance: "Where the Stars Are Closest" is a childhood-memory song — its after-school "Apollo program" and footprints forming a constellation mirror the flashback Honami shares of the four girls first bonding as grade-schoolers on a lost-puppy hunt in the forbidden forest. Its refrain that once-unreachable stars are now right there captures how far Leo/need has grown between that memory and their WAVING-BOX success. The images of each instrument's sound becoming a guiding landmark resolve into the ending's pressure-free jam session, where they rediscover music made purely for themselves.

EVENT|0204-stay-solid-no-fold.resonance: "Soar" is a declaration of self-authored identity — its insistence that the singing voice is a language spoken with bare feet planted on the ground, and that this voice cannot fall silent because the singer was thrust into the world "as myself," mirrors VBS refusing to become Douglas's manufactured commodity. The lyric about casting off a stifling, hollow "freedom" to walk toward genuine hardship reframes the group's choice to reject a corporate shortcut and carve their own path. That philosophy is exactly what the team voices in Episode 7's climax, even as the song's battered-but-still-climbing imagery foreshadows Douglas privately branding their independence a threat.

EVENT|0205-great-yell-for-dreamers.resonance: "Dreamer's Beat" opens by lamenting how everything curdled into scores and results — the exact penalty-system, deadline-driven pressure crushing the dancer Raise — then pleads to be reminded of the joyful, self-forgetting days of pure creation. That plea is the story's engine: the four members help Raise recover the joy of dancing and the wish to make others want to dance too. The song's returning heartbeat rhythm and the "initial impulse" that still rings true mirror the ending, where Minato admits he wants Raise's genuine, infectious dance and the two rehearse as true equals.
EVENT|0205-great-yell-for-dreamers.attribution: English translation by [[User:SunnySkiesTLs|SunnySkiesTLs]], proofread by [[mh:vocaloidlyrics:User:Violet330|Violet330]]. Can only be used in accordance to the restrictions stated on her [https://rentry.co/SunnySkiesTLs Rentry].

EVENT|0207-into-the-new-light.resonance: "Return to the road" frames renewal as resuming a journey — its refrain of not leaving but going home, getting back to the trip, mirrors the video-club girl choosing not to give up but to return to filmmaking on her own terms. The song's charge to stop fearing change because "that style itself is the answer" tracks Mafuyu revealing her hidden self to convince the girl her own voice is worth pursuing. Its bittersweet lines urging a companion to change and keep walking even down a separate path land on the ending, where the girl quits the toxic club, founds her own, and her healed fragment blooms into a wholly new Sekai.
EVENT|0207-into-the-new-light.attribution: English translation by [[User:MK The Misery Kid|MK The Misery Kid]], proofread by [[User:SunnySkiesTLs|SunnySkiesTLs]] and Violet330. May only be used in accordance to the restrictions stated on their [[User:MK The Misery Kid#Translation TOS|user page]].

EVENT|0208-phantom-maze-monster.resonance: "All in One" voices Tsukasa's breakdown from the inside — the beloved voice curdling into a curse, the inability to meet expectations, and the urge to disappear mirror the dissociation his method-acting descent into childhood resentment triggers. The turn where bandmates insist "I'm here" and he grabs the outstretched hand is Episode 7's intervention by Emu, Nene, and Rui reaffirming their eternal bond. Its thesis — embrace hope and despair alike, throw nothing away, and carry even the wounded self from back then — is exactly the integration that lets him deliver a balanced, powerful final performance.
EVENT|0208-phantom-maze-monster.attribution: English translation by [[User:SunnySkiesTLs|SunnySkiesTLs]]. Can only be used in accordance to the restrictions stated on her [https://rentry.co/SunnySkiesTLs Rentry].

EVENT|0209-aidoru-hanazato-minori-yume-n.resonance: "Gimme more!" is a bright idol manifesto whose core promise — being your idol who will make you shine and bring another smile tomorrow — is precisely the hope-giving identity Minori grows into across her documentary week. The disarming line "Me? Really? Is it okay for me to be your favorite?" captures the humility beneath her charm, the same quality that wins over the film crew. Its fall-then-rise-again refrain and the sense of having grown stronger through others resolve at the ending, where she handles a swelling crowd of fans as One-day Police Chief with composure and realizes she is truly becoming an idol who delivers hope.
EVENT|0209-aidoru-hanazato-minori-yume-n.attribution: Official English translation retrieved from the [https://youtu.be/p1BHscS8O5w Original MV].

EVENT|0210-ase-nai-ima-wo-sai-tte.resonance: "Light" aches with impermanence — its lines about time pressing on, an uncertain future, and one another's voices perhaps growing rarer name the very reason Ena and Mizuki plan the trip: their paths will eventually diverge, so they must treasure the now. The song's insistence that these clumsy, fleeting days all sparkle and are "treasures" worth remembering into an unseen future mirrors Ena filling her sketchbook to preserve each moment. Its resolve to keep living strongly and move toward tomorrow while gazing at that light matches both the title's coloring of an unfading present and the closing beach fireworks where the group reflects on their bond.
